messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert: aggregated 5xx rate 18% on model-service-eu for release/v5.2.0 (canary group)
maya: seeing it on dashboards too — latency is fine but error responses spike with tokenizer errors in logs
liam: oncall here, paging in. which canary hosts are affected?
jen: canary hosts: eu-canary-01/02/03. stack traces show 'TokenizerMismatchError: unexpected token id' and 'weight load checksum mismatch' in the same window
sam: that sounds like a packaging problem — two different artifacts drifted: model weights v5.2.0 vs tokenizer v5.1.7
raj: confirmed via s3 manifests: weights uploaded with tag v5.2.0 but tokenizer.json points to v5.1.7 due to CI race during release
maya: customer impact: traffic routed 5% to canary by default; some EU customers hitting generation failures (~12k requests/min affected)
customer-success-bot: pinging CS for customers in eu-west-1 with high error rates, creating support cases where needed
liam: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag to disable v5.2 canary rollout 2) route canary traffic back to stable 3) hotfix tokenizer file on hosts
jen: prefer fast and safe: kill-switch the canary flag, route traffic to stable model, then investigate hotfix
sam: agreed. prep command to flip flag:

```
# disable canary rollout for v5.2
redwoodctl flags set models.v5.rollout.enable=false --env hosted --reason "canary tokenizer/weights drift"
```

maya: rolloff initiated by liam? please confirm when done
liam: running now.
opsbot: Executing flag update: models.v5.rollout.enable -> false by liam
opsbot: Flag update success (propagated to edge routers in ~30s)
maya: monitoring metrics — canary traffic drops to 0% :eyes:
sam: starting to route canary hosts back to stable instances, adding a fallback route for requests currently in-flight
raj: I'll snapshot manifests and pin tokenizer->weights mapping to avoid CI race repeating. pushing a CI gate for manifest diff check
jen: customer impact update: errors dropping, 5xx rate back to baseline in ~2m :white_check_mark:
customer-success-bot: notifying affected customers: email drafts queued, priority support assigned to open cases
liam: quick postmortem notes: root cause = release pipeline race that allowed inconsistent artifacts into the canary bundle (weights and tokenizer out of sync). severity: high for subset of canary traffic, not full-prod due to rollout size
maya: next steps: (a) complete rollback & verify all canary hosts return to stable (b) add CI manifest checksum gate (c) create runbook addendum for model release kill-switch and postmortem
sam: I'll take (a) and (b). raj owns (c) with release-engineering
jen: handoff — liam, I'm going offline in ~20m. can you continue as primary? i'll be on pager if needed
liam: taking over primary on-call. ping me in thread for anything urgent
opsbot: Incident resolved -> mitigation: flag flip + route rollback; incident tag applied: model-canary-config-drift
maya: filing incident report doc and linking to runbook PR: https://redwood.infra/reports/1857654321-canary-drift
raj: PR for CI gate opened: https://git.redwood/infra/ci/merge-requests/412
sam: follow-up action: schedule a canary re-run with a deterministic artifact build next deploy, do not enable automatic canaries until CI gate is green
jen: thanks team. postmortem draft requested in 48h. closing thread for now but keep monitoring for any related regressions
incident-bot: Reminder: add severity, timeline, and mitigation to the incident report within 4 hours.
